sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Describe two main functions of the Chief Minister.
questions.answer: (1) advises the Governor on the appointment of Council of Ministers and allocation of portfolios to them; presides over the meetings of the State Council of Ministers and also coordinates the functioning of different ministers; (2) The Chief Minister is required to communicate to the Governor all the decisions of the Council of Ministers. is the sole link of communication between the Council of Ministers and the Governor. It is he/she who formulates the policies and guides the Council of Ministers to implement them.

questions.q: Describe any two legislative powers of a Governor.
questions.answer: (1) He/She addresses the State Legislative Assembly or the joint sessions of the two houses of the legislature. However, the Governor may dissolve the Assembly earlier on the advice of the Chief Minister. (2) He/She also nominates one-sixth of the members to the Legislative Council, if the State has a bi-cameral legislature. A bill passed by the State Legislature becomes a law or Act only when the Governor gives assent to it. He/She can reserve any bill passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President of India.

questions.q: Explain any two qualifications for a Governor of an Indian State.
questions.answer: (1) Every citizen is related to and influenced by the governments functioning at both the levels. In order to become a Governor, a person must have the following qualifications. (ii) The candidate for the post of the Governor should have the age of: (a) 18 years 23 years (c) 30 years (d) 35 years. should have held a judicial office in the territory of India for at least 10 years; or (2) He/she must not hold any office of profit; a member of Parliament, a State Legislature or a Council of Ministers who becomes Governor must give up that seat.

or.q: Explain any two powers of the Chief Minister of a State.
or.answer: (1) He/she forms the Council of Ministers by advising the Governor and allocates and can change portfolios. (2) presides over the meetings of the State Council of Ministers and also coordinates the functioning of different ministers; is the sole link of communication between the Council of Ministers and the Governor. The primary function of the State Legislature is law-making.

questions.q: Which qualifications are required to be a judge of a High Court? Explain any two.
questions.answer: (1) Every citizen is related to and influenced by the governments functioning at both the levels. In order to become a Governor, a person must have the following qualifications. He/She is appointed by the President of India. (2) should have held a judicial office in the territory of India for at least 10 years; or should have been an advocate in one or more High Courts for at least ten years continuously without break.

questions.q: Differentiate between civil cases and criminal cases.
questions.answer: Civil Cases: These cases filed in civil courts pertain to disputes between two or more persons regarding property, breach of agreement or contract, divorce or disputes between landlords and tenants. In such civil cases, the court does not award any punishment as violation of law is not involved. Criminal Cases: Such cases relate to theft, robbery, rape, pick-pocketing, physical murder etc. These cases are filed in the criminal courts by the police, on behalf of the State, against the accused. In such cases, if the court finds the accused guilty, he/she is awarded punishment.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any three executive powers of the Governor of a State.
questions.answer: (1) He/ She appoints the Chief Minister and other members of the Council of Ministers. He appoints only that person as Chief Minister who is the Leader of the majority in the Legislative Assembly. (2) He/She also appoints persons on important posts such as the Chairpersons and Members of the State Public Service Commission, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission and the Advocate General, Judges of the courts, other than the High Court. (3) He/she is consulted on the appointment of High Court judges; all executive action is taken in his/her name, though on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Explain the executive and legislative powers of the Governor.
questions.answer: (1) At the state level, there is a Governor in whom the executive power of the State is vested by the Constitution. He/ She appoints the Chief Minister and other members of the Council of Ministers. He/She also appoints persons on important posts such as the Chairpersons and Members of the State Public Service Commission, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission and the Advocate General, Judges of the courts, other than the High Court. (2) Legislative: summons and prorogues the legislature and dissolves the Assembly, addresses it, nominates members to the Council (and earlier one Anglo-Indian to the Assembly), and gives assent to bills, returns them or reserves them for the President.

questions.q: 'The Chief Minister is the head of the government in the State and plays a very important role.' Support with examples.
questions.answer: (1) He/she chooses ministers and allocates portfolios (e.g. who handles education or police). (2) presides over the meetings of the State Council of Ministers and also coordinates the functioning of different ministers; It is he/she who formulates the policies and guides the Council of Ministers to implement them. Many times States also adapt Union Governments welfare schemes and implement them. (3) He/she communicates all decisions to the Governor and is praised or blamed for everything that happens in the State; with a clear majority he/she is very powerful, though in a coalition partners limit the role.

questions.q: Describe the legislative functions of the State Legislature.
questions.answer: (1) A Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly is sent to the Legislative Council which has to pass it or to return it with recommendations to the Legislative Assembly.If the Legislative Assembly passes that Bill once again either with recommendations of the Council or without those, it shall be deemed to have been passed by both the Houses. (2) As regards, Money Bills, these can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly. After the Assembly passes the Money Bill, it goes to the Legislative Council which has to pass it or return the Bill to the Assembly with its recommendations within 14 days of the receipt of the Bill. (3) He/She cannot withhold the assent on the Money Bill but can send back an ordinary bill for reconsideration or can reserve any of the bills for consideration by the President.

questions.q: Explain the functions of the State Legislature.
questions.answer: (1) We are all guided by the laws made by state and union legislatures, administered by both the governments and get justice from courts at both the levels. (c) Financial Powers: You must have read in the newspapers that every year the budget is presented by the government in the Legislature for its approval. After the Assembly passes the Money Bill, it goes to the Legislative Council which has to pass it or return the Bill to the Assembly with its recommendations within 14 days of the receipt of the Bill. The two houses of the State Legislature are: Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. (2) Control over the executive — the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Assembly and can be removed by a no-confidence motion; questions and adjournment motions keep a check. (3) Another one-third members are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly; (c) Electoral Functions: The elected members of the Legislative Assembly are members of the Electoral College for the election of the President of India. The members of the Vidhan Sabha also elect the members of the Rajya Sabha from their respective States. (d) Functions related to Constitutional Amendments: There are important functions of the State Legislature related to the amendment of the Constitution.

questions.q: Explain the jurisdiction of a High Court.
questions.answer: (1) The High Court exercises original jurisdiction for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and other legal rights. The High Court may also hear election petitions under its original jurisdiction challenging election of a member of State Legislature. (2) Appellate jurisdiction: hearing appeals against judgments of district judges in civil cases and sessions courts in criminal cases (over seven years' imprisonment); confirming death sentences. (3) High Courts may also punish for contempt or disrespect of the Court. In addition to this, the State Legislative Assembly also controls the Council of Ministers.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the powers and position of the Governor of a State.
questions.answer: (1) Executive powers: appoints the Chief Minister and ministers, the Advocate General and heads of State commissions. (2) Legislative powers: summons, prorogues and dissolves the legislature, addresses it, nominates members, and assents to or returns bills or reserves them for the President. (3) In fact, the budget i.e. ‘the Annual Financial Statement’ of the State is prepared and presented by the State Finance Minister before the State Legislature, on behalf Moreover, no money bill can be introduced in the State Legislature without the recommendations of the Governor. He/She also has control over the State Contingency Fund. (4) Discretionary powers: chooses the CM when no party has a majority, reserves bills for the President, and reports for President's Rule under Article 356. (5) But the Governor acts as a nominal head, and the real executive powers are exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister. Normally, the Governor exercises all his/her powers on the advice of the Council of Ministers. (6) Secondly, the Governor acts as a link between the Centre and the State. be correct to say that the Governor is just a constitutional or ceremonial head. He/ She can exercise his/her powers effectively under certain circumstances, especially when there is political instability in the State. Since he/she is a link between the Centre and the State, he/she becomes very effective, if the central government sends directions to the State government.

questions.q: Explain the composition of the State Legislature and how it keeps control over the executive.
questions.answer: (1) As we have seen above, the State executive consists of the Governor, the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers. In most of the States it is unicameral i.e. has only one house. The two houses of the State Legislature are: Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. (2) The Assembly has 60–500 directly elected members for five years; MLAs must be 25. (3) The Council (not more than one-third of the Assembly, at least 40) is permanent: one-third elected by local bodies, one-third by MLAs, one-twelfth by graduates, one-twelfth by teachers, one-sixth nominated; members serve six years. Control: (4) Even if the Assembly rejects the recommendations of the Council, it will be deemed to have been passed by both the Houses. The Council of Ministers is responsible to Vidhan Sabha collectively. The Council of Ministers is removed, if the Vidhan Sabha adopts a motion of no-confidence against it. However, a Chief Justice or a Judge can resign. (5) Moreover, The State Legislature keeps checks on the government by asking questions and supplementary questions, moving adjournment motions and calling attention notices. (6) (c) Financial Powers: You must have read in the newspapers that every year the budget is presented by the government in the Legislature for its approval. Moreover, no money bill can be introduced in the State Legislature without the recommendations of the Governor. After the Assembly passes the Money Bill, it goes to the Legislative Council which has to pass it or return the Bill to the Assembly with its recommendations within 14 days of the receipt of the Bill.
